'''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' (北野天神社, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto Shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture|1=Saitama Prefecture}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa, Saitama|en|Tokorozawa, Saitama|qid=Q165857|lt=Tokorozawa City|1=Tokorozawa, Saitama}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Motomachi|1=Kotesashi Motomachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11460790}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class according to the system of the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}), with its former Ranking under the modern shrine Ranking system being that of a {{ill|Kensha|ja|県社|1=Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kensha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}.

The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55523456}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmantenjinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is a collective term for these shrines.<ref>{{Cite web|and=|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title=北野天神社（きたのてんじんしゃ）（北野） |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>

== {{nihongo|Worshipped deities|祭神|Saijin}} ==
* {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (もののべてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Kushitama Nigi Hayahito|lt_ja=饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Mononobe Tenjinsha" within the system; it is enshrined together with {{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|1=Izumoiwai Shrine, Moroyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30933323}}.
* {{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55523456}} (くにいちぎじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Yachihoko no Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Kuniichi Jigisha" ({{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|1=Izumoiwai Shrine, Moroyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30933323}} is enshrined together).
* {{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmantenjinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (てんまんてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}.

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shuinjo|1=shuinjō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11093673}} to the shrine.
* The Mononobe Tenjinsha was the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mujashi Kunizukuri|1=Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11504612}} for the family) and continues to enshrine their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}.
* As a Tenjin Shrine, it was first enshrined by {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Shūsei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a 5th-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}, in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|en|Chōtoku|qid=Q1327213|lt=Chōtoku|1=Chōtoku}} era (995) as a guardian in his capacity as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi-no-Mori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵国司|1=musashikokushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11546337}}, sent from Kyoto's {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|en|Kitano Tenmangū|qid=Q662176|lt=Kitano Shrine|1=Kitano Tenmangū}}. Subsequently, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie|1=Minamoto no Yoshiie}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|en|Ashikaga Takauji|qid=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji|1=Ashikaga Takauji}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|qid=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie|1=Maeda Toshiie}}.
* Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|qid=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō|1=Kyōhō}} era (1722), an opening ceremony ({{ill|Shukkai-chō|ja|出開帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shukkai-chō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 開帳|1=Kaichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6347588}}) for the shrine's sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, temple treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the behest of the shogun.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>

== Shrine Grounds ==
Within the shrine precincts, a sanmichi (approach path) lined with {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|qid=Q234731|lt=torii|1=Torii}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/stone lanterns|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 灯籠|1=Stone lantern|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q12012294}} is located on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|en|Kamakura Kaidō|qid=Q2389309|lt=Kamakura Kaidō|1=Kamakura Kaidō}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the haiden (worship hall).

; Shrines Within the Grounds
* {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|1=Inari shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q514480}}
* {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|1=Aviation Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30319396}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|en|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|qid=Q5694703|lt=Tokugawa Yoshitoshi|1=Yoshitoshi Tokugawa}}, at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokorozawa Army Airfield|1=Tokorozawa Airfield|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11658682}}. Its establishment was inspired by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|qid=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine|1=Yasukuni Shrine}}; it was thus determined that a guardian deity for national aviation should be enshrined. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|en|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|qid=Q2822344|lt=Army Air Officer Academy|1=Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Air Base|en|Iruma Air Base|qid=Q3015843|lt=Iruma Base|1=Iruma Air Base}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its present grounds.
* {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579708|1=Ayako Tenjin Shrine}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|Wet nurse|en|Wet nurse|qid=Q472898|lt=wet nurse|1=Wet nurse}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tajihi Fumiko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
* {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Jinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579709|1=Kotesashi Shrine}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area.

; Trees on the Grounds
* {{ill|Mikotozakura|ja|尊桜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikotozakura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru|1=Yamato Takeru}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|Noda|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noda|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).
* {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainagon Ume|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|qid=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie|1=Maeda Toshiie}}, currently the second generation as of 2015. It is said that Maeda Toshiie, who claimed descent from {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}} and used the Ume crest ({{ill|Ume Crest|ja|梅紋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ume Crest|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウメ|1=Prunus mume|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q157763}}), revived the shrine by planting a single plum tree during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】; his title at that time was {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|qid=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon|1=Dainagon}}.
; Other Elements Within the Grounds
* A stone monument recording the origin of the local name "Kitano" – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 18 (2006). Although recent land reorganization has changed the shrine's address to Kotesashi Motomachi, the surrounding area retains the name "Kitano" as derived from this shrine.
* The camp site of {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|qid=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince|1=Prince Munenaga}}.
* A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently (in the 2010s) rebuilt with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dragon|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竜|1=Dragon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q7559}}.
* A kaguraden (dancing hall).
* A stone marker.
* The sacred horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinme|qq=}}).

; Trees and Other Features
* The "Mikotozakura" cherry tree – Said to have been planted by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru|1=Yamato Takeru}}, this tree repeatedly dies and regrows.
* The "Dainagon Ume" – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|qid=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie|1=Maeda Toshiie}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named for Maeda Toshiie's former Rank, {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|qid=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon|1=Dainagon}}, and commemorates his revival of the shrine during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】.
* A stone monument (addressed "Kitano") – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 18 (2006); it notes that the surrounding area "Kitano" derives its name from the shrine.
* The camp site of {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|qid=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince|1=Prince Munenaga}}.
* A hand-washing basin (temizuya) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a dragon.
* A kaguraden (dancing hall).
* A power stone.
* A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinme|qq=}}).

=== Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible Cultural Property:
** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|en|Kyōwa|qid=Q960763|lt=Kyōwa|1=Kyōwa}} era (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>
** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=北野天神社中世文書 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>

== List of Festivals ==
* New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – Ritual talismans ("祈祷札") are distributed.
* Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1)
* Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed.
* Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed.
* Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed.
* Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed.
* Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed.
* Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed.
* Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at the Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods.
* Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 and main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed.
* Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Annual musical offerings and a village kagura are performed biennially.
* Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=北野天神社のお祭り |publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine |accessdate=2022-01-15}}</ref>

[[File:Kitano-Tenjin-sha sandō.jpg|thumb|Kitano Tenjin Shrine, South Approach Path]]
'''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' ({{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenjin Shrine|1=Kitano Tenjinsha (Tokorozawa)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11404275}}, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|qid=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture|1=Saitama Prefecture}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa, Saitama|en|Tokorozawa, Saitama|qid=Q165857|lt=Tokorozawa City|1=Tokorozawa, Saitama}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Motomachi|1=Kotesashi Motomachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11460790}}. It is classified as a Shikinaisha (as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}; two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class), and under the former modern shrine Ranking system it held the Rank of Prefectural Shrine.

The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55523456}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmantenjinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is the collective term for these shrines.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenjin Shrine|1=Kitano Tenjinsha (Tokorozawa)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11404275}} (Kitano) |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the Edo period, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shuinjo|1=shuinjō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11093673}} to the shrine.
* The Mononobe Tenjin Shrine served as the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mujashi Kunizukuri|1=Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11504612}} for details on the clan) and still enshrines their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}.
* As a Tenjin shrine, it was established in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|en|Chōtoku|qid=Q1327213|lt=Chōtoku|1=Chōtoku}} era (995) when {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Shūsei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}, was commissioned as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi-no-Mori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵国司|1=musashikokushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11546337}} from Kyoto’s {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|en|Kitano Tenmangū|qid=Q662176|lt=Kitano Tenmangu|1=Kitano Tenmangū}}; thereafter, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie|1=Minamoto no Yoshiie}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|en|Ashikaga Takauji|qid=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji|1=Ashikaga Takauji}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|qid=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie|1=Maeda Toshiie}}.
* Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|qid=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō|1=Kyōhō}} era (1722), an opening ceremony for the shrine’s sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, shrine treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the shogun’s behest.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>

== Shrine Grounds ==
The shrine grounds feature an approach path lined with {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|qid=Q234731|lt=torii|1=Torii}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/stone lanterns|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 灯籠|1=Stone lantern|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q12012294}} on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|en|Kamakura Kaidō|qid=Q2389309|lt=Kamakura Kaidō|1=Kamakura Kaidō}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the area in front of the haiden (worship hall).

; Shrines Within the Grounds
* {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|1=Inari shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q514480}}
* {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|1=Aviation Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30319396}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|en|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|qid=Q5694703|lt=Tokugawa Yoshitoshi|1=Yoshitoshi Tokugawa}} at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokorozawa Army Airfield|1=Tokorozawa Airfield|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11658682}}. Its establishment was prompted by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|qid=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine|1=Yasukuni Shrine}}. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|en|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|qid=Q2822344|lt=Army Air Officer Academy|1=Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Air Base|en|Iruma Air Base|qid=Q3015843|lt=Iruma Base|1=Iruma Air Base}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its current grounds.
* {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579708|1=Ayako Tenjin Shrine}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|Wet nurse|en|Wet nurse|qid=Q472898|lt=wet nurse|1=Wet nurse}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tajihi Fumiko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}.
* {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Jinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135579709|1=Kotesashi Shrine}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area.

; Trees on the Grounds
* {{ill|Mikoto-zakura|ja|尊桜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikoto-zakura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru|1=Yamato Takeru}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|nodate|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/nodate|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).
* {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainagon Ume|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|qid=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie|1=Maeda Toshiie}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named after Maeda Toshiie’s former Rank, {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|qid=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon|1=Dainagon}}, commemorating his restoration of the shrine during the {{ill|Siege of Odawara|en|Siege of Odawara|qid=Q4372123|lt=Odawara Campaign|1=Siege of Odawara}}.
; Other Elements Within the Grounds
* A stone monument recording the origin of the local name “Kitano” – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 18 (2006); it states that the surrounding area “Kitano” derives its name from this shrine.
* The campsite of {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|qid=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince|1=Prince Munenaga}}.
* A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dragon|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竜|1=Dragon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q7559}}.
* A kaguraden (dancing hall).
* A power stone.
* A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinme|qq=}}).

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible Cultural Property:
** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Consisting of 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi, with 7 old logs |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>

=== Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible Cultural Property:
** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|en|Kyōwa|qid=Q960763|lt=Kyōwa Era|1=Kyōwa}} (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>
** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Medieval Documents |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}}</ref>

== List of Festivals ==
* New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – "Prayer talismans" ("祈祷札") are distributed.
* Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1)
* Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed.
* Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed.
* Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed.
* Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed.
* Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed.
* Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed.
* Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods.
* Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 (yo-miya) and the main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed.
* Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Musical offerings are made annually, and a village kagura is performed every two years.
* Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Festival|publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine |accessdate=2022-01-15}}</ref>
